contexts: 600-bed teaching hospital, about 380 colorectal resections a year
seven-element bundle adopted two years ago
active 30-day surveillance with a day-30 phone call
reading: Infection follows from patient risk (emergency surgery, contamination, stoma, diabetes, obesity), from operation length and from which bundle elements were actually delivered. Emergency cases have both more infection and less compliance, so an unadjusted comparison would credit the bundle with the difference between emergency and elective surgery. Elements travel together, so element-level estimates are unstable. Half of the outcome happens after discharge, and patients living alone are the hardest to reach.

summary: Map shows emergency status as the main confounder and post-discharge follow-up as the main measurement risk.
